title: Systematic Optimization of Sputtered AZO Thin Films and Their Integration as Alternative Transparent Electrodes for Perovskite Solar Cells
authors: Zeynep Mavili; Mücahit Yılmaz
affiliations: Necmettin Erbakan University; Necmettin Erbakan University
abstract: Abstract Transparent conducting oxides (TCOs) are critical components of perovskite solar cells (PSCs), motivating the search for low-cost and scalable alternatives to conventional fluorine-doped tin oxide (FTO). Among the proposed alternatives, Al-doped ZnO (AZO) has been widely investigated as a low-cost, indium-free transparent conductive oxide. However, systematic studies correlating sputtering parameters with AZO thin film properties and PSC performance through direct benchmarking against commercial FTO under identical device fabrication conditions remain limited. In this study, AZO thin films were systematically optimized by magnetron sputtering through controlled variation of sputtering power, annealing conditions, substrate temperature, and deposition duration. The optimized high-temperature-grown AZO film (AZO-13) exhibited high visible transparency (∼86%), low sheet resistance (1.26 × 101 Ω·sq–1), strong preferential (002) orientation, and high calculated electrical conductivity (∼9.85 × 102 S·cm–1), achieving a Haacke figure of merit (0.668) that slightly surpassed that of commercial FTO (0.664). To evaluate its applicability as a transparent electrode, the optimized AZO film was directly integrated into PSC devices and compared with commercial FTO under identical fabrication conditions. The AZO-based PSC achieved a stabilized efficiency of 16.49%, while comparative PL/TRPL, EQE, and EIS analyses revealed that the lower device performance mainly originated from increased interfacial resistance and less efficient charge extraction. In addition, AZO exhibited improved long-wavelength transparency compared with FTO, suggesting potential relevance for tandem-oriented photovoltaic applications. These results establish a clear process–structure–property–device relationship for sputtered AZO thin films and demonstrate their potential as alternative TCO electrodes for PSC technologies.

title: Tailoring the properties of Er-doped IZO thin films via controlled RF magnetron co-sputtering for photovoltaic applications
authors: Mohsin Khan; Qasim Ali; Rashid Ali; Muhammad Bilal Asif; Ghazi Aman Nowsherwan; Mahrukh Shafeeq; Saira Riaz; Mansun Chan; Shahzad Naseem
affiliations: University of the Punjab | Hong Kong University of Science and Technology; University of the Punjab; Ghulam Ishaq Khan Institute of Engineering Sciences and Technology; Hong Kong University of Science and Technology; University of the Punjab; University of the Punjab; University of the Punjab; Hong Kong University of Science and Technology; University of the Punjab
abstract: Abstract Er-doped indium zinc oxide (Er–IZO) thin films were deposited on glass substrates via radio-frequency magnetron co-sputtering, maintaining 90 W RF power on the IZO target while varying the Er DC power at 20, 30, and 40 W. XRD analysis showed that moderate Er incorporation (30 W) produced the largest crystallite size (31.76 nm), whereas excessive doping (40 W) reduced the coherence length to 28.40 nm due to increased lattice distortion. UV-VIS spectroscopy confirmed > 80% visible transparency for all samples, with the optical bandgap increasing from 3.28 eV (pristine) to 3.43 eV (20 W) and 3.80 eV (30 W) via the Burstein–Moss effect. A slight bandgap reduction to 3.50 eV at 40 W is attributed to defect-induced carrier compensation and enhanced scattering, which also caused minor transmission losses. Photoelectron spectroscopy revealed a non-monotonic work-function evolution: an initial decrease from 4.18 to 3.92 eV at 20 W, a modest increase to 3.94 eV at 30 W, and a larger rise to 4.32 eV at 40 W, driven by dopant clustering, carrier trapping, and electronic-structure modification. These results highlight the delicate balance between dopant incorporation, lattice integrity, and electronic behavior that governs the optimization of Er-doped IZO thin films as photovoltaic-relevant transparent conducting and optoelectronic materials.
